finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the user-supplied `target` query parameter straight to http.Get. There is no validation of scheme, host or resolved IP. An attacker can make the server request internal services, loopback addresses or cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/, and the response body is returned to the caller (full-read SSRF).
finding.source: r.URL.Query().Get("target") at main.go:15 (HTTP query parameter on /fetch)
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response body copied to the client at main.go:22

trace.note: /fetch is registered on the public listener at :8080
target is read from the query string without any check
http.Get(target) is issued; the default client also follows redirects
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. The `allowed` host map is only used in safeFetch, not in fetch. There is no scheme check, no IP or private-range filtering, and no custom dialer. No authentication middleware is registered.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param `target` unvalidated to http.Get and main.go:22 returns the body, /fetch is registered at main.go:41 with no auth or middleware, and the `allowed` check exists only in safeFetch (main.go:27).
